fixes.explanation: Nothing in these verses says the camp is moving, friend. The reason Moses gives is, “For today the LORD will appear to you.” (Leviticus 9:4). Setting out isn't mentioned at all. The offerings are about the LORD appearing.

That's right. Moses tells Aaron to sacrifice his own sin offering and burnt offering to make atonement for Aaron and for the people (Leviticus 9:7). So Aaron's offerings reach past Aaron. Then Moses adds the people's offering, which is also to make atonement for them.

Moses says both, friend. In Leviticus 9:7 he tells Aaron to sacrifice his own sin offering and burnt offering to make atonement for Aaron and for the people. So the people are included from the start. Then Moses adds the people's offering, which is for them as well.

Yes, the horns. Aaron's sons bring him the blood, and he dips his finger in it and applies it to the horns of the altar (Leviticus 9:9). The rest he pours out at the base of the altar. I think dipping a finger with that much riding on it takes a steady hand, and mine would be shaking.

Right, outside the camp. The fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver go up in smoke on the altar, but the flesh and the hide get burned up outside the camp (Leviticus 9:10-11). So one calf ends up in two places. Same calf, two addresses.

Right. Aaron took a handful of the grain offering and burned it on the altar, in addition to the morning's burnt offering (Leviticus 9:17). Only a handful, not the whole thing. The text doesn't say what becomes of the rest.

Yes. Aaron's sons bring the fat portions from the ox and the ram, and they place them on the breasts (Leviticus 9:19-20). Then Aaron burns the fat portions on the altar. So the fat rides on top of the breasts first, and then it goes to the fire.

Yes. Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them (Leviticus 9:22). He had made the sin offering, the burnt offering and the peace offering, and then he stepped down. The blessing comes right as he finishes. I think that's a lovely way to close it out.

Yes. Fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar (Leviticus 9:24). The fire comes from the LORD's presence. When all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell facedown. I dive face-first into chocolate chips for fun, but I bet this is a better reason to hit the ground.
